units.sentence: **Input · Dec 14, 2026, 9:30 a.m.:** Send any public comment to the PSC by this time, 24 hours before the Dec 15 session where it is scheduled to vote.
units.marker: {computed: comments are due 24 hours before a vote (P-030); the Dec 15 session starts at 9:30 a.m. (P-024), so a comment sent by 9:30 a.m. on Dec 14 is on time even if the vote comes first}
units.problem: The tag does not source its premise that the PSC votes on this case at the Dec 15 session. P-024 only lists 'Dec 15 9:30 am Administrative Session'. The link to Docket 57171 comes from P-013 (a Final Decision on Dec 15 at the regularly scheduled Administrative Session). This is a citation gap only; the premise is true.
units.suggested_fix: Add P-013 to the tag, e.g. {computed: comments are due 24 hours before a Commission vote (P-030); the PSC decides this case at the Dec 15 Administrative Session (P-013), which starts at 9:30 a.m. (P-024), so a comment submitted by 9:30 a.m. on Dec 14 is on time even if the vote comes first}
units.reason: Recomputed: Tue 2026-12-15 09:30 minus 24 hours = Mon 2026-12-14 09:30 (same time zone, no clock change). The vote cannot come before the session opens, so 9:30 a.m. Dec 14 is at least 24 hours before any vote in that session, and the 'even if the vote comes first' logic holds. P-030: 'Comments must be submitted 24 hours before a Commission vote.' P-024: 'Dec 15 9:30 am Administrative Session'. P-013 and P-029 confirm the decision is made at that session.

framing_issues.text: Send any public comment to the PSC by this time
framing_issues.issue: P-030 says comments must be 'submitted' 24 hours before a vote. 'Send ... by this time' (and 'sent' in the tag) could lead a reader to mail a comment on Dec 14 that arrives too late. Use 'Submit' / 'submitted'.

framing_issues.text: 24 hours before the Dec 15 session where it is scheduled to vote
framing_issues.issue: The home page does not mention that the PSC takes up this case earlier, at the Dec 10 Energy Committee meeting starting 9:30 a.m. (P-012: 'This matter shall be considered'; P-024). The passages call Dec 15 the 'Final Decision' (P-013) and do not say any vote happens Dec 10, so the Dec 14 time is correct under P-030. But a comment submitted after the Dec 10 meeting reaches the PSC after the committee has taken up the case, and if any Commission vote were taken Dec 10, P-030's rule would point to Dec 9, 9:30 a.m. Consider adding the Dec 10 committee meeting, with an {editorial} suggestion to comment by Dec 9, 9:30 a.m. to be safe.
